Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
27-y/o (DOB 09 May 2016 recorded) male with 1-week sore throat and dry cough, now mild exertional dyspnea, seeks reassurance, treatment advice, and sick note.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sore throat ×1 week → dry cough after 1–2 days → mild shortness of breath 3–4 days ago.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent wheeze, “a bit” of chest pain (see conflict), initial low-grade fever first 3 days (resolved), intermittent headaches, reduced appetite (no weight loss).  
• Pertinent negatives: No sputum, no hemoptysis, no nasal/sinus congestion, no rash.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Allergies: Peanuts (no medication allergies).  
• Medications: None.  
• Family history: Mother – lung cancer.  
• Social: Non-smoker (rare experimental use); no recent long-haul travel; lives in UK (US-born); unclear asbestos exposure; works (details not given).

Examination:
• No physical examination or vitals documented.

Impression:
Likely self-limiting viral upper respiratory tract infection with reactive cough and mild exertional dyspnea.

Plan:
• Reassurance: Low likelihood of tuberculosis or lung cancer given current presentation; symptoms expected to improve within 4–5 days.  
• Symptomatic care: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), adequate fluids, rest.  
• Red-flag advice: Seek in-person GP review or urgent care if breathlessness suddenly worsens, becomes concerning at rest, or if overall condition deteriorates.  
• Follow-up: Contact medical professional if no improvement or worsening after 4–5 days.  
• Documentation: Sick note provided for additional days off work.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: Vitals, physical examination findings (e.g., throat, chest auscultation), medication reconciliation beyond patient’s statement, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially reports chest pain and wheeze, later doctor states “you say you don’t have any chest pain” – conflict noted. Shortness of breath initially denied then affirmed.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational overlaps, no significant inaudible sections.
